topics.title: Doggerland: The Stone Age Land the Sea Drowned
topics.core_question: How much land did the rising sea swallow as the last ice age ended, and how do we know people lived on it?
topics.why_they_click: A whole inhabited landscape sits under the North Sea, and fishing nets keep dragging up its bones and peat.
topics.data_source: British Geological Survey North Sea seabed mapping; peer-reviewed Doggerland studies (Gaffney et al.); NOAA sea-level reconstructions
topics.evidence: "ice age explained" is the fastest-rising search term in the dossier, up 1680% over five years.

topics.title: Why Ice Ages Run on a 100,000-Year Clock
topics.core_question: What sets the planet's ice-age rhythm, and why does the 100,000-year beat still not fully match the theory?
topics.why_they_click: Tiny wobbles in Earth's orbit pace the ice, but the biggest cycle is the one the maths explains worst.
topics.data_source: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology; NASA orbital-cycle explainers; peer-reviewed ice-core and Milankovitch studies
topics.evidence: "ice age explained" is up 1680% over five years, the strongest rising signal available.

topics.title: Hunga Tonga 2022: The Eruption That Circled the Earth
topics.core_question: What made the January 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption send a pressure wave around the world and water into the stratosphere?
topics.why_they_click: An eruption that broke the ocean surface and rang the planet's atmosphere like a bell, captured on satellite from the first second.
topics.data_source: NASA Earth Observatory; NOAA satellite and pressure records; Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program
topics.evidence: "volcano eruption explained" is rising, up 283% over five years.

topics.title: The 1811 Earthquake That Made the Mississippi Run Backwards
topics.core_question: Why did a series of great earthquakes strike the middle of a continent in 1811-1812, and what does the record say about the hazard there today?
topics.why_they_click: The largest quakes east of the Rockies hit a frontier almost nobody was watching, and eyewitnesses said the river reversed.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program New Madrid studies; USGS historical earthquake accounts
topics.evidence: Serves both "biggest earthquake in history" (up 47%) and "plate tectonics explained" (up 571%) as an intraplate mystery.

topics.title: Toba: The Supervolcano That Blocked the Sun
topics.core_question: What did the Toba supereruption roughly 74,000 years ago do to the climate, and did it really push early humans through a bottleneck?
topics.why_they_click: The largest known eruption of the last 100,000 years, with a live scientific argument over how much damage it actually did.
topics.data_source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program; peer-reviewed Toba tephra and climate studies
topics.evidence: "supervolcano" is rising, up 38% over five years, and the debate gives the video a genuine unsettled question.

topics.title: Why the Mariana Trench Is 11 Kilometres Deep
topics.core_question: How does one plate bending under another carve the deepest place on Earth, and what does that same process do at the surface?
topics.why_they_click: The deepest point on the planet is a side effect of the same subduction that produces the largest earthquakes and tsunamis.
topics.data_source: NOAA Ocean Exploration bathymetry; USGS subduction zone research; peer-reviewed Challenger Deep depth measurements
topics.evidence: "plate tectonics explained" is up 571% over five years, the second-strongest rising term.

topics.title: Pinatubo 1991: The Eruption That Cooled the Earth
topics.core_question: How much did the 1991 Pinatubo eruption cool the planet, and how did scientists predict the cooling before it showed up in the temperature record?
topics.why_they_click: A single eruption measurably dropped global temperatures for two years, and the forecast of it was one of volcanology's cleanest wins.
topics.data_source: USGS Volcano Hazards Program and Pinatubo reports; NASA Earth Observatory stratospheric aerosol records
topics.evidence: "volcano eruption explained" is rising, up 283% over five years.

topics.title: The Younger Dryas: When the World Froze Again
topics.core_question: What sent the Northern Hemisphere back into near-glacial cold around 12,900 years ago, and why do scientists still argue about the cause?
topics.why_they_click: The thaw was interrupted for more than a thousand years, and the competing explanations include an ocean shutdown and a contested impact.
topics.data_source: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology; peer-reviewed Younger Dryas and North Atlantic circulation studies
topics.evidence: "ice age explained" is up 1680% over five years, and the unsettled cause satisfies the rule on naming disagreement.

topics.title: Lisbon 1755: The Quake That Invented Seismology
topics.core_question: How did the earthquake, tsunami and fire that destroyed Lisbon in 1755 change both European thought and the way we study earthquakes?
topics.why_they_click: Three disasters in one day, on a holy day, in a city of churches, that forced Europe to ask what the ground actually is.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program historical earthquake catalogue; peer-reviewed 1755 Lisbon earthquake and tsunami studies
topics.evidence: "biggest earthquake in history" is rising, up 47% over five years.

topics.title: The 1964 Alaska Quake: Four Minutes of Shaking
topics.core_question: What did the magnitude 9.2 Alaska earthquake of 1964 do in four minutes, and how did it teach scientists how megathrusts behave?
topics.why_they_click: The second-largest earthquake ever recorded, whose ground measurements are still the reference for how a great fault breaks.
topics.data_source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program; Alaska Earthquake Center (University of Alaska Fairbanks)
topics.evidence: "biggest earthquake in history" is rising, up 47% over five years, and this is the strongest record not already covered.
